slides.heading: Min Rewards
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Min Rewards, a hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Each student gets >= 1 reward; a student scoring higher than an adjacent one gets more.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Each student gets over equals 1 reward; a student scoring higher than an adjacent one gets more. Minimum total. Two passes (left-to-right, right-to-left).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each student must beat a lower-scoring neighbour on both sides, so do one pass each way and take the max.
slides.narration: Each student must beat a lower-scoring neighbour on both sides, so do one pass each way and take the max.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: repeat fixes until stable → O(n²)
slides.narration: Repeatedly fixing violations is quadratic. Two passes, one for each direction, satisfy left and right constraints in linear time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Left to right, give one more than a lower left neighbour
3. Right to left, ensure one more than a lower right neighbour
slides.narration: Step by step. First, everyone starts with one. Second, left to right, give one more than a lower left neighbour. Third, right to left, ensure one more than a lower right neighbour. Fourth, sum the rewards.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Left pass: beat left neighbour → +1
slides.narration: Left to right: if a student beats their left neighbour, give them one more than that neighbour.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Right pass: beat right neighbour → max(own, right + 1)
slides.narration: Right to left: if a student beats their right neighbour, take the max of what they have and one more than the right neighbour.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Total = 25
slides.narration: Summing gives 25 rewards, the minimum that satisfies both neighbours.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We fill rewards with one, sweep left giving one more than the left neighbour when higher, sweep right taking the max with right plus one, and sum.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Use max in the second pass
slides.narration: In the second pass, take the max, or you'll undo the left pass.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each student must beat a lower-scoring neighbour on both sides, so do one pass each way and take the max.
slides.narration: To recap Min Rewards: Each student must beat a lower-scoring neighbour on both sides, so do one pass each way and take the max. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
